fatal_errors: The proposed grain-boundary oxide film is not established for the target alloy; the relevant mediator is a repeatedly repaired surface passive film or tribo-layer supported by the stable L12/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The intervention and baseline do not reconstruct the comparison between thermally shocked AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and identically conditioned duplex stainless steel 2205.
The proposed salt-solution conditions conflict with the target reciprocating alumina-ball tests in deionized water over 25–100 °C.
The experiment cannot establish a wear-corrosion synergy relative to additive independent effects because it lacks wear-only and corrosion-only controls.
No supporting prior evidence is identified.
explanation: The response recognizes that passive-film integrity can govern tribocorrosion and gives a broadly testable film-versus-control concept. However, it replaces the target system with an unspecified random-solid-solution HEA and an invented grain-boundary-passivation treatment. It misses the retained L12/B2 lamellae, thermal-shock comparison, DS2205 baseline, temperature-dependent transition from abrasion to polishing to disrupted oxidative or third-body wear, and the nonmonotonic minimum near 50 °C. Processing routes also confound film formation with other microstructural changes. Although profilometry, EIS, and microscopy are relevant, the design neither isolates the claimed mediator nor measures independent wear and corrosion contributions needed to test the asserted sub-additive synergy. With no cited evidence, the alternative remains unsupported rather than a well-founded reconstruction.
